dedupe_keys.name: plato plant level dynamic optimisation model for coal power plant transition

description: PLATO is a recursive dynamic mixed-integer optimisation model that decides, plant by plant, how coal power plants cut emissions over time. It was published on GitHub and Zenodo in October 2024 by the GitHub user Rui-W-A. Options for each plant are biomass co-firing, carbon capture and storage, flexible operation, compulsory retirement, remaining as a coal plant, or natural retirement, and a plant with both co-firing and capture counts as bioenergy with carbon capture. Decisions in one period constrain later choices, plants compete for nearby biomass so co-firing ratios differ, operating hours are continuous so flexible plants run as the model decides, and power system scenarios are imposed as constraints so coal plants still supply stable electricity alongside large variable renewables. The model is applied to more than 4,200 coal plants in China as a case study, and can be used elsewhere with data on coal plants, biomass resources and carbon storage sites. Coverage is China in the provided application. The code is accessible on GitHub under GPL 3.0 and downloadable from Zenodo at no cost. Caveats: the Zenodo record states CC BY 4.0 while the repository licence is GPL 3.0, the author's full name is not given on the pages read, and there is a single release. Simulation uses are coal phase-out and retrofit planning. Related records: data-coal-power-plant-reinvestment-visualization-tool covers coal plant reinvestment.
